I'm not really understanding this patch.

I'm in full support of trying to eradicate copies, I'm just not sure this one does.  Lets move it away from shared_from_this, and it will be a lot more apparent whether we're making a copy or not.

Agreed to use the explicit copy when necessary.
However, how can handle if we want to keep it rather than copying it during the needed scope and lifetime?

The current code is always copying 'request body` at least if "If-Match:" is specified. (I don't think it is necessary for the case)

> Agreed to use the explicit copy when necessary.
> However, how can handle if we want to keep it rather than copying it during the needed scope and lifetime?
> 
> The current code is always copying 'request body` at least if "If-Match:" is specified. (I don't think it is necessary for the case)

Generally you would do this with a std::move().

In this case, callback is set so that it can be invoked as a handler of the object of `req` later.
Because it is defined as `(const Request &req)` and it may be completed earlier than callback, it is done by creating a shared_ptr of req.copy.  

I don't think it is the intention to copy it but there is no way around with the current code logic.

As an example, in other code, `req` was passed as `&req` to validatePrivilege 

 - https://github.com/baemyung/bmcweb/blob/7e9093e625961f533250a6c193c1a474e98007c4/http/routing.hpp#L1368C4-L1368C5  

```
   void validatePrivilege(Request& req,
        ```)
    {
        crow::connections::systemBus->async_method_call(
            [this, &req, asyncResp, &rule,
```
However, its lifetime can't be hold until all async calls are completed.

- 
So, it is changed to `[req{std::move}]` via https://github.com/baemyung/bmcweb/commit/915d2d4e59be56958b04a79ba96e0242ef735f44, but it still not work. So go partially back via https://github.com/baemyung/bmcweb/commit/d3c8ce63ce13b2094b01f7c9eb8be4d3d5daa52f

- 
Eventually it is fixed by https://github.com/baemyung/bmcweb/commit/102a4cdacb0a6d8c8c3c97e10bedbb66000ac5dc
but it causes the duplication if "If-Match:" is passed.

In other words, the goal is not necessarily to copy, but to hold its lifetime for Request in this case.

Please also take a look at my other responses.

Enable shared from this isn't needed unless we want to manage the lifetime of this class from within the class.  I don't think we want to enforce that:

A. All request structs are shared_ptr
B. A request class manages its own lifecycle.


Request structure does no IO.  It shouldn't manage it's own pointer lifetime.

Currently, 
- all incoming Request structs are already `shared_ptr<crow::Request>` - https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/ef0b2d46d0245447bf21d6c74821599d5f7b7b05/http/http_connection.hpp#L925.


- They are referenced as `crow::Request` during as a part of route handling
https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/ef0b2d46d0245447bf21d6c74821599d5f7b7b05/http/routing.hpp#L662.

It  is essentially a de-referenced object from `shared_ptr<crow::Request>` to match with the existing codes that are specified like `routeXXX(..., const crow::Request& req, ...)` .

In other words, in bmcweb,  most cases (I think all cases), `crow::Request` are created/managed as std::shared_ptr<Request>.

S, I don't think that using `enable_shared_from_this<Request>` causes the extra overhead.


- In addition, there may be cases to capture `req` - e.g. https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/74938/69/redfish-core/lib/redfish_sessions.hpp#328.  This seems not easy to avoid.
If we use shared_ptr, the object can be captured as `shared_from_this()` rather than copying.

Yes, all requests are in shared_ptr now, but again, this request object does no IO, it should not be managing its own complex lifetime.  FWIW, this is why there's a distinction made between AsyncResp and Response, one is a shared_ptr that always handles lifetime, and the other does not.
Const_cast is banned for a reason.  if there are issues in const-ness that aren't part of our usage of a third party library, lets just fix them.

This is used because
`req->shared_from_this()` gives `std::shared_ptr<const crow::Request>`.
However, most of places are using as `std::shared_ptr<crow::Request>`.

I think this was a reason to keep the previous codes as `const crow::Request` in routing.hpp.

Ideally, if we pass `std::shared_ptr<crow::Request> req` all-way thru in doing routes, this back conversion (`const Request&` to `const shared_ptr<Request>&` via 
 const_cast) wouldn't be needed.
However this would cause many changes of BMCWEB_ROUTE and called functions.

> This is used because
> `req->shared_from_this()` gives `std::shared_ptr<const crow::Request>`.

It only returns that if the value coming in is const.  There are two overloads:
https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/memory/enable_shared_from_this/shared_from_this

I'm not sure that's what we want to do, but if we need to, that's preferable to const_cast
I'm very surprised this code doesn't crash.  req is not a shared pointer, so pulling shared_from_this should make a copy?

I don't think this is causing a crash, as the original `req` is kept in lifetime by capturing its original form (`shared_ptr<Request>`) via bind_front() and shared_from_this().


I think the issues(we've seen before) related to `Request` are due to the lifetime of `Request` for the async-call (e.g. validatePrivilege() in older code) and caller.
- how to hold `Request` lifetime inside or outside of the async calls.

It was resolved by making it as shared_ptr<Request> - https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/71006.
However, since it did not change `setUpRedfishRouteWithDelegation(const crow::Request& req)` and all places from the previous `route(const Request& req)` to `route(const std::shared_ptr<Request>&)`.

As the result, this setUpRedfishRouteWithDelegation() & handleIfMatch() also need to deal with `const Request&` by copying it.
If it were passed as `const std::shared_ptr<Request>&`, it would not need to copy it, but it can be handled by capturing it without copying.
